facts.claim: SSE from a Next 16.4.3 App Router Route Handler works with a plain Response(ReadableStream) + TextEncoder. Verified on the standalone build, Node 26.13.0: first bytes arrive in ~2 ms and one event per second arrives at 1.0 s spacing, even with Accept-Encoding: gzip. The docs only show the ReadableStream pattern, not SSE.
facts.source: Next bundled docs node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md (Streaming section). Test app: <scratch>/ssetest (raw-socket timing, curl). Not tested through Caddy.

facts.claim: request.signal 'abort' fires when the client disconnects, in the standalone server with the compression middleware on. Four curl -m disconnects logged four 'ABORT CLEANUP' lines. ReadableStream.cancel() did not log in that run, so register both cleanups.
facts.source: Empirical, ssetest/server.log (same test app).

facts.claim: GET Route Handlers are dynamic here. A GET handler with no dynamic export built as 'ƒ' (dynamic) in 16.4.3. The project also uses connection() because of the nonce proxy.
facts.source: Empirical: next build output for /api/nodyn in ssetest. Project: <repo>/src/app/layout.tsx.

facts.claim: Next 16.4.3 has built-in gzip, on by default. router-server.js runs compression() unless config.compress === false, and pipe-readable.js calls res.flush() after every chunk, so compressed streams are flushed per write. In my test, Route Handler responses were NOT compressed: DEBUG=compression logged "[ 'text/event-stream' ] not compressible" and "[ 'text/plain' ] not compressible" (a 5 KB text/plain also stayed uncompressed), while the prerendered page was gzipped. The cause is that the Content-Type reaches the middleware as an array. That is an implementation quirk, not a documented guarantee.
facts.source: node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-server.js lines 142-145 and 318-326; node_modules/next/dist/server/pipe-readable.js lines 80-85 and 188-192; docs 01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/compress.md (default gzip, disable with compress:false); DEBUG=compression run on ssetest.

facts.claim: The compression middleware Next bundles skips responses whose Cache-Control contains no-transform (shouldTransform regexp). Verified: SSE with 'no-cache, no-transform' returned normally.
facts.source: node_modules/next/dist/compiled/compression/index.js (shouldTransform); ssetest /api/stream-nt.

facts.claim: Module-level singletons are NOT shared between instrumentation.ts register() and a Route Handler in the 16.4.3 standalone build. A module-level counter incremented by register() read 0 in the route; the same counter on globalThis read 5, then 9. register() is documented as called once per server instance, before the server is ready.
facts.source: Empirical: ssetest instrumentation.ts + lib/bus.ts + app/api/bus/route.ts. Docs: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/instrumentation.md (register runs once; process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME guard).

facts.claim: Next self-hosting docs only say proxies such as nginx must disable buffering for streaming, with X-Accel-Buffering: no as the example. Caddy does not use that header.
facts.source: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/self-hosting.md, 'Streaming and Suspense' (line ~213).

facts.claim: Caddy reverse_proxy flushes immediately when the response has Content-Type: text/event-stream (also Incremental: ?1, or unknown Content-Length). flush_interval is ignored in that case. A negative flush_interval (-1) 'does not cancel the request to the backend even if the client disconnects early', so it would defeat request.signal cleanup.
facts.source: https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy (flush_interval), raw: github.com/caddyserver/website src/docs/markdown/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy.md lines 432-437.

facts.claim: Caddy encode default match is an allowlist that includes 'header Content-Type text/*', so text/event-stream is encoded by default. Response matchers support only 'status' and 'header' (a '!' prefix on the field means the header must be absent). There is no negation for a value match, so you cannot write 'text/* except event-stream'. The default minimum_length is 512. Docs say SSE responses are exempt from the threshold and are streamed as written.
facts.source: https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/encode (match, minimum_length); response-matchers.md (status, header); upstream issue caddyserver/caddy#6293 states there is no way to negate.

facts.claim: Caddy SSE+encode behaviour by version. Up to and including v2.11.4, encode withheld response headers until the first body write. A first write under 512 bytes meant the stream stayed uncompressed, and a first write over 512 bytes meant it was gzip/zstd with a flush per event. Commit df44d6c3 ('encode: flush headers immediately for server-sent events', fixes #6293, 2026-07-31) is contained in v2.11.6 and v2.11.7, and NOT in v2.10.2 through v2.11.4. From v2.11.6, SSE headers go out immediately and SSE is still compressed by default.
facts.source: GitHub API compare for tags v2.10.2 to v2.11.7 against df44d6c3; modules/caddyhttp/encode/encode.go at v2.11.4 (FlushError and Write) and master; issue caddyserver/caddy#6293.

facts.claim: Response 'Cache-Control: no-transform' does NOT stop Caddy's encode in released versions. In v2.10.2, v2.11.4 and v2.11.7, isEncodeAllowed(r.Header) inspects the request's Cache-Control. A change to honour the response header (a72377a1, 2026-10-31) is on master only, after v2.11.7.
facts.source: modules/caddyhttp/encode/encode.go at tags v2.10.2, v2.11.4, v2.11.7 (isEncodeAllowed called with r.Header); commit a72377a1 'encode: ignore request no-transform' is ahead of v2.11.7 per GitHub compare.

facts.claim: The way to exclude SSE from encode is routing, not a matcher. 'handle' blocks are mutually exclusive, and a 'handle' with no matcher is the fallback. Directive order puts header and request_body before encode, handle and reverse_proxy.
facts.source: https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/handle; directives.md directive-order list. I did not run caddy validate (no caddy binary here, and pulling an image needs your OK).

facts.claim: Caddy defaults relevant to long SSE streams: no WriteTimeout (0), IdleTimeout 5m, Read/WriteIdleTimeout 1m (HTTP/2 health checks). A 15 s keep-alive comment, or a data event every ~5 s, keeps the connection active. Default protocols are h1, h2 and h3.
facts.source: caddyserver/caddy v2.11.7 modules/caddyhttp/app.go lines 921-940 and server.go line 543.

facts.claim: React 19.3.0 (2026-09-09) stable ships <ViewTransition /> and addTransitionType. Installed react@19.3.1 exports ViewTransition (typeof 'symbol') and addTransitionType (function).
facts.source: facebook/react CHANGELOG.md 19.3.0; node -e require('react') in <repo>.

facts.claim: Next 16.4.3 needs NO next.config flag for view transitions. The docs say they 'work in the App Router with no configuration'. Setting experimental.viewTransition prints 'Unrecognized key(s) ... viewTransition at "experimental"' (the key is gone). Route navigations are Transitions, so <ViewTransition> animates on <Link>/router navigation. Link takes transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}, and router.push/replace accept transitionTypes too.
facts.source: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md; docs link.md (transitionTypes prop, line ~509); empirical next build with experimental.viewTransition in ssetest.

facts.claim: ViewTransition rules from the Next docs. Plain setState does not trigger it; only Transitions, Suspense and useDeferredValue do. Put wrappers in each page.tsx, not layout.tsx (layouts persist, so enter/exit never fire). Shared-element morphs only form when the destination renders in the same commit as the navigation (prefetched pages). Browser back/forward and router.refresh() carry no transition type. Add '::view-transition { pointer-events: none }' or clicks during the animation are lost. Disable animation under prefers-reduced-motion via CSS, because React does not do it automatically.
facts.source: view-transitions.md (same file); react.dev ViewTransition reference ('Always check prefers-reduced-motion'), raw reactjs/react.dev src/content/reference/react/ViewTransition.md.

facts.claim: Browser support (MDN BCD 8.1.8, published 2026-11-02). document.startViewTransition and view-transition-name: Chrome/Edge 111, Safari 18, Firefox 144. view-transition-class: Chrome/Edge 125, Safari 18.2, Firefox 144. ViewTransition.types (transition types): Chrome/Edge 125, Safari 18.2, Firefox 147. Next's docs say that without support the app works normally and the transitions just do not animate.
facts.source: npm @mdn/browser-compat-data@8.1.8 data.json (api.Document.startViewTransition, css.properties.view-transition-class, api.ViewTransition.types); Next view-transitions.md note.

facts.claim: CSP: no change needed for view transitions. React sets view-transition-name through CSSOM (el.style.viewTransitionName = ...), and MDN says property assignment via CSSOM is not blocked by style-src-attr. Only setAttribute('style') and cssText are blocked. Inline style attributes in SSR HTML are already covered by the project's style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'. EventSource is governed by connect-src, and the current connect-src 'self' already covers a same-origin /api/v1/stream. proxy.ts excludes /api/ from the matcher, so the SSE route gets no CSP header, which is fine for a non-HTML response.
facts.source: node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js lines 16393-16394, 16958-16963; MDN content csp/style-src-attr and csp/connect-src (EventSource listed); <repo>/src/proxy.ts.

facts.claim: <details> animation support (BCD 8.1.8). ::details-content: Chrome/Edge 131, Firefox 143, Safari 18.4 (Safari cannot chain pseudo-elements after it, WebKit bug 283446). interpolate-size and calc-size(): Chrome/Edge 129 only. Firefox (bug 1945962 / 1896734) and Safari (WebKit 295132 / 274177) have not shipped them, and BCD flags both as experimental. Chrome's article gives the pattern: ::details-content { height:0; overflow:clip; transition: height .5s, content-visibility .5s allow-discrete }, with 'interpolate-size: allow-keywords' and '[open]::details-content { height:auto }' inside @supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords).
facts.source: npm @mdn/browser-compat-data@8.1.8 (css.selectors.details-content, css.properties.interpolate-size, css.types.calc-size); https://developer.chrome.com/blog/styling-details

facts.claim: Recharts 3.10.1 (npm latest, 2026-11-02). Line, Area, Bar and Tooltip isAnimationActive defaults to 'auto': off in SSR and honours prefers-reduced-motion. Line defaults are animationDuration 1500, animationEasing 'ease' and animateNewValues true. Bar defaults are 400 ms and animationMatchBy 'append'. Since 3.9, Line/Area/Bar take animationMatchBy, with exports matchByIndex (default for Line), matchAppend and matchByDataKey(key). matchByDataKey pairs old and new points by payload key, which suits sliding time windows. The default index matching pairs by array position, so a sliding window makes every point wobble. Line matching interpolates matched points and slides added/removed points in or out. The charts accept a 'responsive' boolean prop (ResponsiveContainer without a wrapper). XAxis supports type='number', scale (including 'time') and domain, and BarChart supports layout='vertical'.
facts.source: npm pack recharts@3.10.1: types/cartesian/Line.d.ts, Bar.d.ts, Tooltip.d.ts, types/util/types.d.ts (responsive, line ~1284), es6/animation/matchBy.js, es6/cartesian/Line.js lines 62-115, types/index.d.ts line 120.

facts.claim: I did not benchmark 1,500 points. The only grounded levers are dot={false}, Tooltip isAnimationActive={false}, a short animationDuration, a fixed number-axis domain, and fewer points. I make no measured claim for the 1,500-point case.
facts.source: Not measured; Recharts d.ts props only.

facts.claim: EventSource semantics (WHATWG HTML 9.2). The initial reconnection time is implementation-defined, 'probably in the region of a few seconds'. 'retry: <ASCII digits>' sets it in ms, otherwise it is ignored. On a network error or when the stream ends, the browser fires 'error', waits the reconnection time (possibly with extra backoff), then reconnects. If the last event ID string is non-empty it sends Last-Event-ID, which is set by 'id:' lines (ignored if the value contains NUL). The browser FAILS the connection, with readyState CLOSED and no reconnect, when the response status is not 200, the Content-Type is not text/event-stream, or the error is an aborted network error. HTTP 204 is the documented way to tell a client to stop reconnecting. A comment line every ~15 s is advised against legacy proxies. The request uses cache mode no-store.
facts.source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html (9.2.2 constructor steps, 9.2.3, 9.2.4, 9.2.5, 9.2.7, 9.2.10).

facts.claim: Consequence for deploys. While the container restarts, Caddy answers 502 (non-200), so the browser's EventSource goes CLOSED permanently and never retries. The page must watch for readyState === EventSource.CLOSED and create a new EventSource with backoff. A manually created new EventSource starts with an empty last event ID, so it sends no Last-Event-ID. Pass a ?since=<ts> parameter on manual reconnects.
facts.source: WHATWG 9.2.2 and 9.2.3 (same URL); Caddy 502 on upstream failure is standard behaviour, not tested here.

facts.claim: Concurrency. The 6-connections-per-origin SSE limit is an HTTP/1.1 limit. Over HTTP/2 the limit is the negotiated max concurrent streams (MDN: 'defaults to 100'). RFC 9113 recommends the value be 'no smaller than 100'. Caddy does not override it: caddyhttp/server.go at v2.11.7 has no MaxConcurrentStreams setting. Go's http2 server default is 250 (x/net http2/server.go defaultMaxStreams = 250), and stdlib HTTP2Config documents 'at least 100'. For HTTP/3, quic-go's DefaultMaxIncomingStreams = 100. If a client falls back to h1 the 6-connection cap applies, which is why each tab should open exactly one shared stream.
facts.source: MDN using_server-sent_events (warning box); https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.txt SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS; golang/net http2/server.go line 62; golang/go src/net/http/http.go HTTP2Config; quic-go internal/protocol/params.go line 34; caddy v2.11.7 server.go.

recommendations: Transport: one SSE endpoint, GET /api/v1/stream, one EventSource per tab. Mount the EventSource in a client provider in the root layout so /mac, /vm and /compare share it and route changes do not reconnect. Send 'retry: 5000', then an immediate ': connected' comment, then a snapshot event. Use 'id: <epoch-seconds of the reading>' on each event so Last-Event-ID can replay readings missed since that id from SQLite. Send a ': ka' comment every 15 s (data every ~5 s already keeps it alive).

Fan-out: the sampler (started from instrumentation.ts register(), guarded by NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') publishes into a bus held on globalThis (Symbol.for key), never in module scope, because module state is not shared with the route handler. The route subscribes and unsubscribes on abort. One timer feeds all subscribers, so connections add no DB or proc reads.

Headers on the SSE response: Content-Type 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8', Cache-Control 'no-cache, no-transform', X-Accel-Buffering 'no' (harmless). Leave Connection: keep-alive out; it is invalid on h2 and Caddy handles hop-by-hop. Also export dynamic = 'force-dynamic' and runtime = 'nodejs'.

next.config: set compress: false. Caddy already does zstd/gzip, so it removes any chance of Next's compression middleware touching the stream (today it skips Route Handlers only through the array Content-Type quirk), and it avoids double compression of HTML. The cost is that 'npm start' on a laptop serves uncompressed.

Caddy: exclude the SSE path from encode with a handle split and do not set flush_interval (see snippet). It works the same on 2.10.x through 2.11.7. Without the split, 2.11.6+ compresses SSE, and 2.11.4 and earlier delay the headers until the first write. Run 'caddy validate' in the container as vm-setup.sh already does, and curl -N the stream afterwards. Which Caddy version the VM runs was not checked.

Client reconnect: handle onerror with readyState === CLOSED by closing, waiting with capped exponential backoff plus jitter, and creating a new EventSource('/api/v1/stream?since=<lastId>'). Also close the stream after the tab has been hidden for ~30-60 s and reopen on visibilitychange to visible, with ?since=. This saves the 512 MB / 1 CPU container from idle viewers. Keep the existing router.refresh() AutoRefresh off the live views.

View transitions: no config. Wrap the content of each of app/mac/page.tsx, app/vm/page.tsx and app/compare/page.tsx in the same <ViewTransition enter/exit keyed by transition type, default='none'>. Tag nav Links with transitionTypes (nav-forward when moving right in tab order, nav-back when moving left). Give the header/tab bar viewTransitionName 'site-header' and neutralise its group animation. Add '::view-transition { pointer-events:none }' and a prefers-reduced-motion block that zeroes ::view-transition-*(*) durations. Expect enter/exit animations rather than shared-element morphs on dynamic pages, because dynamic routes are not fully prefetched. Treat the transitions as progressive enhancement; browsers without support just swap.

Live data animation is Recharts' job, not ViewTransition's: SSE-driven setState does not trigger <ViewTransition>. For SSE ticks every ~5 s use a short Recharts animation (animationDuration 400-600 ms, easing ease-out) with animationMatchBy={matchByDataKey('t')} on each Line so a sliding window glides instead of wobbling. Keep isAnimationActive at 'auto' so reduced-motion and SSR are handled.

Compare view: merge both machines into one array of {t, mac, vm} on a minute-aligned timestamp, as percent of each machine's own capacity (0-100), with null where a machine has no reading. Use XAxis type='number' scale='time' dataKey='t' with a domain pinned to [now - window, now] and allowDataOverflow, and YAxis domain [0,100]. Keep the Mac and VM colours and dash styles distinct, and add a legend or direct labels. Per-core CPU: BarChart layout='vertical', XAxis type='number' domain [0,100] hide, YAxis type='category' dataKey='core', Bar animationDuration 400, barSize fixed.

Point count: downsample server-side to the pixel width (about one point per 4-6 px, e.g. mean per bucket for ranges beyond 6 h) rather than sending raw 1-minute rows for 14 days. Set dot={false}, Tooltip isAnimationActive={false}, and activeDot small. Measure with the real 1,500-point range before committing; I did not.

Details accordions: use the Chrome-documented pattern inside @supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords), with interpolate-size on :root and the [open] block-size: auto. Elsewhere (Firefox, Safari) the open and close are instant with no layout break. Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block that sets transition: none. Do not use calc-size() (same support as interpolate-size, Chrome/Edge only).
Do not add a CSP change; keep connect-src 'self' and the existing style-src-attr. If a Cloudflare or other proxy is ever put in front, re-test streaming then.
avoid: flush_interval -1 on the SSE reverse_proxy: it is redundant (SSE is flushed immediately anyway) and stops Caddy cancelling the upstream request when the client leaves, which breaks request.signal cleanup.
Relying on 'Cache-Control: no-transform' to exclude SSE from Caddy encode: released versions (up to v2.11.7) only look at the request header. It does stop Next's bundled gzip.
Module-level singletons for the sampler/bus (instrumentation.ts and route handlers get separate instances); use globalThis.
experimental.viewTransition in next.config: invalid in 16.4.3 and only logs a warning. Not needed.
Putting <ViewTransition> in layout.tsx (enter/exit never fire there) or expecting it to animate SSE-driven setState.
Assuming EventSource always retries: any non-200 or non-event-stream response (such as Caddy's 502 during a deploy) closes it for good.
One EventSource per chart or per component: use a single shared stream per tab. HTTP/1.1 fallbacks cap at 6 per origin.
Recharts default animationMatchBy ('index') on a sliding time window, and the default 1500 ms Line animation on 5 s ticks.
Relying on interpolate-size or calc-size outside Chrome/Edge, or chaining pseudo-elements after ::details-content (Safari bug 283446).
Connection: keep-alive on the SSE response, and any padding or buffering hacks for proxies; neither is needed with Caddy.
Treating my local result as proof of the Caddy path: I verified Next standalone streaming and cleanup, but did not run Caddy, and the VM's Caddy version is unknown.

facts.claim: The running specs container (uid 1000, read_only, cap_drop ALL, no mounts besides /data) ALREADY sees host-wide /proc/meminfo, /proc/stat, /proc/uptime, and fields 1-3 of /proc/loadavg. Compared at the same instant, MemTotal, MemAvailable, Buffers, Cached, Shmem, SReclaimable, the 'cpu' line, uptime and osrelease (7.0.0-1013-oracle) all matched the host. Docker does not virtualize them. Loadavg fields 4-5 (running/total, last pid) are PID-namespace scoped and differ (container '1/491 500' vs host '6/483 1612120'). Node's os.totalmem() also returns the host's 12504535040. No mount is needed for memory, CPU, load, uptime or kernel version.
facts.source: docker exec specs vs host, on the VM, 2026-11-02 16:2x UTC

facts.claim: 'Used' memory should be MemTotal - MemAvailable. procps-ng NEWS 4.0.1 says 'Used memory is Total - Available'. library/meminfo.c: if MemAvailable==0 use MemFree; if MemAvailable>MemTotal use MemFree; mem_used = MemTotal - MemAvailable, and if that is negative use MemTotal - MemFree. Cached_all = Cached + SReclaimable. free.c prints buff/cache = Buffers + Cached_all. The VM has procps 2:4.0.4-4ubuntu3.2. `free -b` printed used=1314181120 = 12504535040 - 11190353920 exactly, and buff/cache=10326396928 = Buffers 453685248 + Cached 9027162112 + SReclaimable 845549568.
facts.source: https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/-/raw/master/NEWS ; .../library/meminfo.c lines 727-739 ; .../src/free.c ; free -b on VM

facts.claim: Kernel meaning of the fields: MemAvailable is an estimate of memory available to start new applications without swapping, computed from MemFree, SReclaimable, the file LRU lists and the low watermarks. Buffers is raw block-device storage. Cached is the page cache INCLUDING tmpfs and shmem (excluding SwapCached). Shmem is tmpfs plus shared memory, so it is a subset of Cached and is not freed without swap. SReclaimable is the reclaimable part of Slab. KReclaimable includes SReclaimable plus other shrinkable kernel allocations. Show 'cache' = Buffers + Cached + SReclaimable, as free does. This VM has SwapTotal 0 and Shmem about 6 MB.
facts.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst (meminfo section, lines ~1122-1205)

facts.claim: CPU from /proc/stat: the first line is 'cpu user nice system idle iowait irq softirq steal guest guest_nice' in USER_HZ units. getconf CLK_TCK is 100 on the VM. guest and guest_nice are already counted inside user and nice (node_exporter source comment), so total = the first 8 fields. Per-field % = delta_field / delta_total x 100 between two samples. The kernel doc says iowait is unreliable and can decrease, so clamp negative deltas to 0. Show user+nice, system+irq+softirq, iowait and steal separately. The VM line (2 cores, Neoverse-N1) since boot: steal 45202 of 35880003 ticks = 0.126%, iowait 0.32%. A 5 s sample gave steal +1 tick and idle +996 of about 1000 (2 cores x 5 s x 100).
facts.source: proc.rst lines 1585-1621; prometheus/node_exporter collector/cpu_linux.go (guest comment); on the VM head -1 /proc/stat twice 5 s apart

facts.claim: Per-container CPU needs a delta of cpu.stat usage_usec (also user_usec, system_usec; always present), divided by wall microseconds, times 100 = % of one core. cpu.stat also has nr_periods, nr_throttled and throttled_usec when the controller is enabled. The specs cgroup already shows nr_periods 183, nr_throttled 10, throttled_usec 301336 (cpus: 1.0 quota). For memory, memory.current is the cgroup's total usage including page cache. The Docker CLI computes 'no cache' usage for cgroup v2 as memory.current - memory.stat inactive_file. Use the same formula so numbers match `docker stats`.
facts.source: cgroup-v2.rst lines 1143-1166 and 1328-1333; docker/cli cli/command/container/stats_helpers.go calculateMemUsageUnixNoCache; cat of specs cgroup files on VM

facts.claim: Host /proc/net is per network namespace. Inside specs, /proc/net/dev shows only lo and eth0 (eth0 rx 40461 B), and /sys/class/net and /sys/devices/.../net are filtered too (find for enp0s6 under /sys/devices finds nothing). On the VM, as the non-root deploy user, `cat /proc/1/net/dev` WORKS and shows the host namespace: lo, enp0s6 (rx 1312354353, tx 1244414287), br-<id>, docker0 and 6 veth*. /proc/1/net is dr-xr-xr-x root and /proc/1/net/dev is readable by others. Link speed in sysfs is -1 (virtio), so don't show it. Use IMDS networkingBandwidthInGbps 2.0 as the reference ceiling. Counting docker0, br-* and veth* would double-count container traffic, so exclude them (and lo) and pick the physical NIC (enp0s6).
facts.source: on the VM: cat /proc/1/net/dev; docker exec specs cat /proc/net/dev; ls /sys/class/net

facts.claim: Security: the node-image containers on the VM run as one shared host uid (no userns remap), and other containers run as root or another uid. If the specs container gets the whole host /proc, it can read the other same-uid containers' /proc/<pid>/environ, io, maps and smaps_rollup (verified as that uid, with output reduced to byte counts). Root-owned /proc/1/environ was denied. The host /proc is mounted without hidepid, so a whole-/proc mount leaks sibling containers' secrets (environ holds tokens). The proc_pid_environ man page says access is governed by a ptrace PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS check, and same-uid passes it.
facts.source: Verified on the VM with read-only checks; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_environ.5.html

facts.claim: What a non-root user that does NOT own the process can read under /proc/<pid>/ (tested as the deploy user on the specs process, pid 1591871): comm, stat, statm, status (shows Uid 1000, VmRSS 117524 kB, RssAnon 47748 kB, RssFile 69776 kB, Threads 11), cmdline, cgroup, mountinfo, limits and oom_score readable. environ, io, maps and smaps_rollup are Permission denied. Of 193 pids only 5 (ubuntu's own) had readable environ and io. comm for the container node process is the truncated title 'next-server (v'. Names from comm are not reliable for container identity. Per-pid reads are not needed for this feature; cgroup files cover the per-container need.
facts.source: on the VM: ls -l /proc/1/ ; loop of cat over /proc/<specs pid>/{comm,stat,statm,status,cmdline,environ,cgroup,io,maps,smaps_rollup}

facts.claim: `pid: host` is not needed. Every number required (meminfo, stat, loadavg, uptime, statfs, cgroup stats) is readable without sharing the PID namespace. node_exporter's documented container setup uses --net=host --pid=host -v /:/host:ro,rslave --path.rootfs=/host, which is much broader than needed (it needs pid: host for per-process collectors). Docker's bind-mount docs allow a single file or a directory as source, with readonly/ro option. specs on n8n_default is a bridge network (172.18.0.0/16), so network_mode: host is also not an option.
facts.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prometheus/node_exporter/master/README.md (Docker section); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docker/docs/main/content/manuals/engine/storage/bind-mounts.md ; docker network inspect n8n_default

facts.claim: cgroup v2 on the VM: /sys/fs/cgroup is cgroup2fs, Docker cgroup driver is systemd (server 29.2.1, 2 CPUs, MemTotal 12504535040). Controllers: cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids rdma misc dmem. Per-container path is /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-<64-hex-id>.scope/. The scope dir is drwxr-xr-x root. memory.current, memory.stat, cpu.stat, io.stat and pids.current are -r--r--r--, so the deploy user reads them. memory.max is 0644 but root-owned. The root cgroup has NO memory.current (only memory.stat and cpu.stat). Inside the container, /sys/fs/cgroup is a private cgroup namespace (own memory.max 536870912, /proc/self/cgroup '0::/'), so sibling containers need a mount of the host cgroup tree. A read-only bind of /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice (not the whole tree) is enough. Mounting a directory, not a file, means new docker-*.scope dirs appear automatically.
facts.source: on the VM: stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup; docker info; ls -l of the 6 scopes; docker exec specs ls /sys/fs/cgroup

facts.claim: Container names are NOT in cgroupfs (the scope name carries only the 64-hex id). Docker's state directories and socket are root-only or group-restricted for an ordinary user, and the container config files hold env vars. Options to map id to name: (1) a host systemd timer running `docker ps --no-trunc --format ...` as the deploy user (same pattern as the existing autodeploy units) writing a small file to a directory mounted read-only (best); (2) mount the docker socket (no: root-equivalent), a socket-proxy with CONTAINERS=1 (still exposes inspect env, needs an image pull); (3) mount the docker state directory (root-only, exposes env secrets) (no); (4) a static id-to-name list in env (ids change on every deploy) (no). If a timer writes the file, mount the DIRECTORY, not the file: a single-file bind mount keeps the old inode when the writer replaces it by atomic rename.
facts.source: Read-only checks on the VM; docs of the existing autodeploy units

facts.claim: System-level systemd timer on Ubuntu 24.04: systemd 255 (255.4-1ubuntu8.18). The VM has 14 timers, including Ubuntu's own apt-daily, apt-daily-upgrade, fstrim, dpkg-db-backup, e2scrub_all, motd-news and systemd-tmpfiles-clean. /etc/cron.d holds only e2scrub_all. The project's own autodeploy timers use OnUnitInactiveSec=60s with a oneshot service run as the deploy user. Caveat: the systemd.timer man page does NOT mention cron at all (zero matches), so 'replacement for cron' is Ubuntu convention, not a man-page claim. What the man page does say: AccuracySec defaults to 1min and timers coalesce within that window, so set AccuracySec=1s for minute-aligned runs. RandomizedDelaySec defaults to 0. OnUnitInactiveSec=60s drifts by the job runtime, so prefer OnCalendar=minutely (or *-*-* *:*:00) with AccuracySec=1s. systemd.exec has RuntimeDirectory=, RuntimeDirectoryMode= and RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=, which fit /run/specs-host (tmpfs /run, 1.2G, no disk wear).
facts.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/main/man/systemd.timer.xml (AccuracySec, lines ~229-286) ; systemd.exec.xml (RuntimeDirectoryPreserve line 1796) ; systemctl list-timers

facts.claim: Installing a system unit/timer under /etc/systemd/system needs sudo once, which the deploy user has. The service itself can run unprivileged as the deploy user with docker group access.
facts.source: Read-only checks on the VM

facts.claim: OCI IMDS v2: endpoint http://169.254.169.254/opc/v2/instance/ (also /opc/v2/vnics/, /opc/v2/volumeAttachments/), required header `Authorization: Bearer Oracle`; a request without it returns HTTP 403. Useful fields: shape, region, canonicalRegionName, shapeConfig {memoryInGBs, networkingBandwidthInGbps, ocpus}. `image` is only an image OCID, so IMDS does NOT give an OS name. The OS has to come from the host's /usr/lib/os-release (/etc/os-release is a symlink to ../usr/lib/os-release), or from a file the host timer writes. A container's own /etc/os-release is Alpine's. The raw response also carries identifiers (OCIDs, tenant, compartment, display name, custom metadata) that must never be published.
facts.source: https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Compute/Tasks/gettingmetadata.htm

facts.claim: IMDS is reachable from inside a container on the compose network with the header, and BusyBox wget is present at /usr/bin/wget. Any code in a container can therefore read instance metadata, so keep the app's use to an allowlist (shape, region) and never proxy raw IMDS responses.
facts.source: Checked once with a read-only request from the running container; Oracle IMDS doc 'metadata/' entry

facts.claim: Disk: statfs inside the container on /data (volume, same ext4 fs as host /) returns the host root filesystem. fs.statfsSync('/data') gave {bsize:4096, blocks:35276604, bfree:30256521, bavail:30252425}, matching host `df /` (/dev/sda1, 144492969984 B total). Use total = blocks x bsize, used = (blocks - bfree) x bsize, and Avail = bavail x bsize. df's Use% = used/(used+avail). On this VM the reserved gap is only 4096 blocks (16 MB). No mount is needed for disk. /proc/diskstats and /sys/block inside the container also show the host's sda and loop0-7 (not netns-scoped); the cgroup io.stat key '8:0' is sda.
facts.source: docker exec specs node -e fs.statfsSync('/data'); on the VM df -B1 / ; stat -f /

facts.claim: Docker on the VM: `docker ps` shows 6 containers (names and images listed in the snippets). specs runs as user=node, PidMode empty, ReadonlyRootfs true, CapDrop ALL, no-new-privileges, Memory 536870912, NanoCpus 1e9, PidsLimit 200, AppArmor docker-default with 12 maskedPaths, and a single volume mount. Masked paths only affect the container's own /proc, not a path like /host/proc. Docker labels in `docker inspect` contain only com.docker.compose.* (project, service, working_dir, config files), and they are only reachable through the docker API, not cgroupfs. The compose service name for specs is 'web', so names must come from container name, not the compose service. Docker Compose v5.1.0. userns-remap is not enabled (SecurityOptions: apparmor, seccomp builtin, cgroupns), which is why container uid 1000 equals host uid 1000.
facts.source: on the VM: docker inspect specs ; docker info ; docker compose version

facts.claim: No fresh mount is needed for host time or kernel: container clocks and os.release() match the host, and the VM has NTPSynchronized=yes and Timezone Etc/UTC. Host uptime = /proc/uptime field 1 (179767 s at 16:2x, booted 2026-10-31 14:33:53 UTC; btime 1793457233 in /proc/stat). Uptime is already host-wide inside the container. PSI files exist (/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}: cpu some avg10=0.73, memory 0.00, io some 0.01) if a pressure indicator is wanted. Memory pressure plays the role of macOS's 'pressure'.
facts.source: on the VM: timedatectl, uptime -s, cat /proc/pressure/*

recommendations: Mount budget (least privilege): 3 read-only mounts and nothing else. (a) /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice -> /host/cgroup:ro (directory; per-container memory.current, memory.stat, cpu.stat, pids.current). (b) /proc/1/net/dev -> /host/net/dev:ro (single proc file; host NIC counters). (c) /run/specs-host -> /host/run:ro (directory; containers.json and host.json written by a host timer). Read meminfo, stat, loadavg, uptime, statfs and diskstats from the container's own /proc and fs, since they are already host-wide. Keep read_only, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, uid 1000, and do NOT add pid: host or the whole /proc or /sys.

The single-file bind of /proc/1/net/dev is UNVERIFIED because creating a container was off-limits. At first deploy run `docker exec specs head -4 /host/net/dev` and confirm it lists enp0s6. If it fails, fall back to the host timer copying /proc/1/net/dev into /run/specs-host/net-dev (60 s freshness, so rates are per-minute only). Do not fall back to mounting all of /proc: it would expose sibling containers' environ because all node containers share host uid 1000.

Host timer: /etc/systemd/system/specs-host-sample.timer ([Timer] OnCalendar=minutely, AccuracySec=1s, [Install] WantedBy=timers.target) and a Type=oneshot service with User=ubuntu, RuntimeDirectory=specs-host, RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755, RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes, Nice=10 and TimeoutStartSec=20s. The script writes tmp then `mv` (atomic) two files. containers.json is `docker ps --no-trunc --format` reduced to id, name, image (strip any @sha256 digest and registry noise) and State. host.json is {os: PRETTY_NAME from /usr/lib/os-release, kernel: uname -r, arch, shape, region, ocpus, memoryInGBs, networkingBandwidthInGbps} from one IMDS curl with `-m 3 -H 'Authorization: Bearer Oracle'`. One install step with sudo in deploy/vm-setup.sh, idempotent, following the n8n-hub-autodeploy.* precedent. Doing IMDS in the timer means the app never needs network access to 169.254.169.254.

Public-page privacy: the page is public, so apply an allowlist/alias to container names (some container names are internal project names) and never show container ids, image digests, interface names other than a generic 'eth', IPs, the hostname, OCIDs or compose paths. Show shape, region, ocpus, memoryInGBs, kernel and OS from host.json only. If a container name is missing from containers.json (id not yet written), show 'container' plus the first 4 hex chars of the id, or hide it.

Formulas to implement: mem.used = MemTotal - MemAvailable (fallback MemTotal - MemFree if MemAvailable is 0 or exceeds MemTotal); mem.cache = Buffers + Cached + SReclaimable; mem.free = MemFree. Store raw kB x 1024. CPU % per field = clamp(delta_field, 0) / delta(sum of first 8 fields) x 100 across 'cpu' (and cpuN for per-core); report user+nice, system+irq+softirq, iowait, steal, and idle = rest. Net rate = delta bytes / delta wall seconds, with a counter-reset guard (delta < 0 => skip). Container CPU % = delta(usage_usec) / delta(wall us) x 100 (of one core; cap display at the cgroup quota if cpus is set), container mem = memory.current - inactive_file from memory.stat. Disk from fs.statfsSync('/data'). Load = first three fields of /proc/loadavg, normalised by 2 cores for a bar.

Cadence: run the in-process sampler every 5 s, which needs only 3 small proc reads, a handful of cgroup reads and one net/dev read (all virtual files, microseconds). Keep a short in-memory ring and push it over SSE, since a live connection is cheap here. Persist one row per machine per minute (mean of CPU % over the minute, last value for gauges, summed net bytes) with a 14-day prune. 14 d x 1440 = 20160 rows per machine, so SQLite is trivial. Use the fixed counters (cpu ticks, net bytes, usage_usec) so a restart only loses one delta.

Edge cases to handle in the sampler: a container appearing or disappearing between samples (key by id, drop ids with no scope dir, treat a missing file as 'gone'); a cgroup memory.max of the string 'max' (n8n-caddy-1, cloudflared have no limit, so show host total as the limit); first sample after start has no delta (emit null, not 0); /proc/stat guest columns can be zero; MemAvailable on this kernel is present, but keep the fallback; IMDS/host.json missing means hide the shape line, never block the page.

Add a minimal health signal for the VM side: if /host/run/containers.json is older than 3 minutes, show names as 'unknown' and note 'host sampler stale'; if /host/net/dev or cgroup reads throw, degrade that panel only. The page already has an 'age' pattern for the Mac, so reuse it.
avoid: Do not mount the Docker socket (root-equivalent on the host) or a socket proxy that allows /containers/*/json, since inspect returns env vars and tokens.

Do not mount the whole host /proc, /, or /sys, and do not use pid: host. The node containers share one host uid, so the specs container could read their /proc/<pid>/environ, io, maps and smaps_rollup (verified). That includes the INGEST_TOKEN-class secrets.
Do not use network_mode: host to see enp0s6: it breaks Caddy reaching http://specs:3000 on n8n_default and widens exposure.

Do not bind-mount a single file that a host job rewrites (containers.json, host.json): an atomic rename leaves the container holding the stale inode. Mount the parent directory instead. (Single files that are procfs/kernel-owned, such as /proc/1/net/dev, are not replaced.)

Do not compute 'used' as total - free - buff/cache or include cache as used: the right base is total - MemAvailable (procps-ng 4.0.1+, matches `free` on the VM). Do not treat container memory.current as 'used' without subtracting inactive_file, since it includes page cache. Do not read Cached as 'not reclaimable', because it includes Shmem.
Do not sum all interfaces from /proc/1/net/dev: docker0, br-* and veth* are container traffic seen twice (br-<id> rx 1.0 GB mostly mirrors container traffic). Count only the physical NIC.

Do not use os.totalmem()/os.cpus() assumptions for the container's own limits: they report host values (12504535040 B, 2 cpus) while os.availableParallelism() is 1; read memory.max/cpu.max from the cgroup if the app's own limits are ever shown.

Do not use `OnUnitInactiveSec=60s` (drifts by run time) or the default AccuracySec=1min (timers coalesce and fire up to a minute late) for the minute sample. Do not describe systemd timers as a documented 'cron replacement': the systemd.timer man page never says that. Cite the precedent on this VM and Ubuntu's own apt/fstrim timers.

Do not expose raw IMDS output (it includes OCIDs, tenantId, compartmentId, displayName and custom metadata) and do not give containers a reason to call IMDS repeatedly. Do not publish interface names, hostname, container ids or compose working_dir.
Do not change the VM from this research step. Nothing on the VM was changed: all commands were read-only.
